question.text: Within the workbook delta range for a call option, an at-the-money (ATM) call has a delta that is approximately:

explanation.text: The Logic: Call delta lies in the range 0 to +1. Deep out-of-the-money calls have delta near 0 and deep in-the-money calls have delta near +1, so an ATM call sits roughly in the middle of that range, near 0.5. The workbook's symmetric put example, where an ATM put has delta near -0.5, reinforces this midpoint behaviour. The Trap: Delta near 1.0 describes a deep ITM call and delta near 0 describes a deep OTM call. -0.5 is the ATM value for puts (whose delta range is -1 to 0), not calls. Note: Remember the symmetry: call delta runs from 0 to +1 and put delta runs from -1 to 0, so an ATM call is around +0.5 and an ATM put is around -0.5.
